summary.en-US: YouTube's speed keys jump by 0.25x and, without Premium, stop at 2x. This keeps the same keys and removes the limit, with smaller steps where you want them: 2.1x, 2.2x, 2.3x. Adds a speed button to the player and Shorts. Collects no data.

description.en-US:
I watch lectures and talks at around 2.3x. Without Premium, YouTube stops at 2x, and its speed keys move a quarter at a time: 1.75x, 2x, done. So I made this.

It keeps YouTube's own keys, Shift + . and Shift + , and takes the cap off. Above 2x the steps get smaller, 0.1x by default, because that's where a small change decides whether you keep up with the speaker or lose them.

**What it does**

- Speeds from 0.25x to 4x out of the box: 0.25x steps up to 2x, then 0.1x steps.
- Shift + . is faster, Shift + , is slower, R jumps between 1x and your speed.
- A speed button in the player, next to YouTube's own controls. Scroll over it to change speed, or click it for a slider and presets. On Shorts it sits with the top-right controls.
- Hold the mouse down on the video for twice your speed. Let go and you're back. At 1.5x, holding gives you 3x.
- Your speed stays put across videos, ads, tabs and restarts.

**One speed control**

YouTube resets the speed on every new video and ad. The extension sets yours back every time. That also means YouTube's own speed menu can't change it, and neither can another speed add-on. If you pick a speed in YouTube's menu, a bubble shows the speed you're actually at. If you use another speed extension, turn it off for YouTube, or the two will fight.

**Your own steps**

Open the settings from the player panel without leaving the video, or from the toolbar button. You can set:

- the step size below and above a point you choose, as fine as 0.01x
- that point
- the slowest and fastest speed, anywhere from 0.1x to 16x
- up to 8 preset buttons

Slowing down works the same way. For language practice or learning a song, set 0.05x steps below 1x. Firefox keeps voices at their normal pitch at any speed.

**Limits**

- It works on www.youtube.com in desktop Firefox 142 and newer.
- Not supported: YouTube Music, m.youtube.com, Firefox for Android, and YouTube videos embedded on other sites.
- At the live edge of a live stream it leaves the speed to YouTube, because there's nothing ahead to speed through.
- Firefox mutes the sound above 8x. You can raise that limit in about:config; the settings page shows how.

**Privacy**

No accounts, no analytics, no network requests. The extension only has access to youtube.com. It stores your speed and settings in your Firefox profile. YouTube pages load about 30 KB of its code, unminified. The source is on GitHub: https://github.com/Volzhanka63/granular-speed-for-youtube

Not affiliated with YouTube or Google.

release_notes.en-US: Hold the mouse down on the video to play at twice your speed (YouTube's own hold gives a flat 2x). When YouTube's speed menu tries to change the speed, a bubble shows the speed you're really at. Speed keys only act when a video is on the page. Full settings open in the corner like the toolbar popup, without dimming the video, and you can undo Reset and preset removal. Presets outside your range are kept instead of deleted. Keyboard and screen reader support in the player panel. The welcome page now explains how it all works, and the pop-up hint in the player is gone. Fixes: a + button that could lower a value, a cleared field resetting to the default, and the whole-number marks on the settings scale. Full list: https://github.com/Volzhanka63/granular-speed-for-youtube/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md

version.approval_notes: No build step or minification: the submitted files are the source, also at https://github.com/Volzhanka63/granular-speed-for-youtube. To test, open any youtube.com/watch page and press Shift+. a few times, or click the speed button at the start of the player's right-hand controls. The tune icon in that panel opens options.html in an iframe over the page (declared in web_accessible_resources); the content script accepts messages only from that iframe's window and the extension's origin, and the iframe posts only to https://www.youtube.com. background.js only opens welcome.html once, on first install. The settings footer links to this add-on's AMO page.
